appraisal_events.evidence: "Comme tu as l'air fatigué et agité"; his gaze repeatedly touches a painful bottom, "l'idée qu'il avait rompu avec sa maîtresse"; his mother strokes his cheek and calls him "son petit garçon", a tenderness that visibly irritates him and with which she draws him off into the back of the salon.
appraisal_events.explanation: In a drawing room where he has come to pay his respects, Saint-Loup is shown wounded and unsettled by the rupture with his mistress, and then publicly petted and infantilized by his mother, which the narration presents without irony as a real diminishment of his composure.

appraisal_events.evidence: "Mme Swann se trouvant seule et ayant compris que j'étais lié avec Saint-Loup me fit signe de venir auprès d'elle."
appraisal_events.explanation: Having been deliberately cold to him a moment earlier, Mme Swann calls the narrator to her side once she grasps his connection with Saint-Loup, so his link to Saint-Loup wins him admission to her company.

status_effects.explanation: Saint-Loup is locally the one who suffers visibly: his agitation is remarked on aloud, its cause is his dependence on the mistress he has left, and he is reduced to a caressed child in front of the room.
He crosses from the cold distance at which Mme Swann had just held him to being summoned to sit beside her, the boundary moving in his favour on the strength of his tie to Saint-Loup.
